claim: The Pixel 6 Omarchy image is built from a GS101 kernel that contains the device's GPU, Wi-Fi, modem and camera drivers before any phone boot test.
oracle: A source checkout is exactly M8 commit 850061c79264d018317e9f849701f165e138e20c, required driver paths exist, and the merged configuration enables Panfrost/GS101 display, BCM4389 PCIe Wi-Fi, CPIF modem and GS101 camera modules.

user_journey.scenario: The user boots Omarchy, opens an Agent, leaves Wi-Fi coverage, inserts a China Mobile SIM and opens the camera; Android slot A remains the recovery path if a driver stage fails.
user_journey.expected: The desktop starts without the known GPU stall, Wi-Fi and cellular interfaces can be diagnosed independently, and camera enumeration is possible before a capture is attempted. A failed stage leaves USB serial recovery available.

invariants: The source checker is read-only and never changes a kernel tree or phone partition.
Only a named GS101 source baseline is accepted; the current GS201-oriented Omarchy tree is rejected.
Firmware, modem NV, calibration and credentials stay outside the public repository.
gitnexus: The kernel boundary owns device-tree and driver support; the Omarchy device package owns userspace handoff and network diagnostics.
GPU, Wi-Fi, modem and camera are separate gates and cannot be promoted from display-only evidence.
ast: The checker has no write, reboot, flash, module-load or network-configuration operation.
Every required source path and configuration option is checked explicitly.

unit.red: The existing Omarchy kernel tree lacks the GS101 PCIe host, CPIF modem and GS101 MIPI-CSIS paths required by the Pixel 6 hardware.
unit.green: The checker accepts the exact GS101 baseline with the hardware fragment and rejects a wrong commit or missing option.

boundaries: exact kernel source -> merged arm64 config -> kernel/image build
kernel modules and device tree -> Omarchy userspace -> GPU/Wi-Fi/modem/camera devices
evidence: M8 GS101 source and Nura hardware notes provide the reference boundary; Pixel 6 cold boot, mobile data and camera capture remain pending.

limitations: The source check does not prove the device boots or that proprietary firmware is present.
The reference supports front and ultra-wide cameras; the rear GN1 camera remains unsupported.
Cellular support still requires tinycbd, read-only phone partitions and Shannon ModemManager integration.
exit_gate: Build the exact kernel and userspace in an isolated output directory, run static checks, then perform a human-approved slot-B boot with serial recovery and validate GPU, Wi-Fi reconnect, China Mobile registration/data and one supported camera capture.
